title: Concentration terms
bullets: Molarity (M): moles of solute per litre of solution; changes with temperature.
Molality (m): moles of solute per kg of solvent; independent of temperature.
Mole fraction (x): moles of a component ÷ total moles; all mole fractions add up to 1.

title: Henry's law
content: Partial pressure of a gas over a solution is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution. A higher K_H means lower solubility at the same pressure and temperature.

title: Raoult's law
content: For volatile components, each partial pressure is proportional to its mole fraction. For a non-volatile solute, relative lowering of vapour pressure equals the solute's mole fraction.

title: Colligative properties
content: These depend on the number of solute particles, not their nature. The van't Hoff factor i corrects for dissociation (i > 1) or association (i < 1).
formula: ΔTb = iKb·m ; ΔTf = iKf·m ; π = iCRT

title: Non-ideal solutions and azeotropes
bullets: Positive deviation: ethanol + acetone, CS₂ + acetone; A–B attractions are weaker; can form minimum boiling azeotropes.
Negative deviation: phenol + aniline, chloroform + acetone; A–B attractions are stronger; can form maximum boiling azeotropes.
Azeotropes boil at constant composition and cannot be separated by fractional distillation.

title: Galvanic and electrolytic cells
bullets: Oxidation occurs at the anode and reduction at the cathode in both cells.
Galvanic cell: chemical energy to electrical energy; anode is negative.
Electrolytic cell: electrical energy drives a non-spontaneous reaction; anode is positive.
Daniell cell: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq)||Cu²⁺(aq)|Cu(s), E°cell = 1.10 V.

title: Standard cell potential
content: Use standard reduction potentials for both electrodes. E° is an intensive property, so it is never multiplied by the stoichiometric coefficient.

title: Nernst equation at 298 K
content: Q contains product ion concentrations over reactant ion concentrations, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. Pure solids are left out.

title: Gibbs energy and equilibrium
content: A positive E°cell means a negative ΔrG°, so the reaction is spontaneous.
formula: ΔrG° = −nFE°cell = −RT ln K ; log K = nE°cell/0.059 (298 K)

title: Molar conductivity and Kohlrausch's law
content: Molar conductivity rises on dilution while conductivity falls. Each ion makes an independent contribution at infinite dilution.

title: Order and molecularity
bullets: Order: sum of the powers of concentration in the experimental rate law; can be zero or fractional.
Molecularity: number of species colliding in an elementary step; always a whole number.
Units of k: (mol L⁻¹)^(1−n) s⁻¹ for overall order n.

title: First order reaction
content: The half-life does not depend on initial concentration.

title: Zero order reaction
content: Concentration falls linearly with time, and half-life is proportional to initial concentration.

title: Arrhenius equation
content: Rate constants rise with temperature because more molecules have energy equal to or above Ea.

title: Pseudo first order reactions
content: These have higher molecularity but behave as first order because one reactant is in large excess.
bullets: Acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate.
Inversion of cane sugar.

title: Transition elements
content: These have partly filled d orbitals in the atom or a common ion. General configuration: (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻².
bullets: Zn, Cd and Hg have d¹⁰ in the ground state and common ions, so they are not regarded as transition elements.
They show variable oxidation states, colour, paramagnetism and catalytic activity.

title: Spin-only magnetic moment
content: n is the number of unpaired electrons. Remove 4s electrons before 3d when forming the ion.

title: Lanthanoid contraction
content: Size falls steadily across the lanthanoids because 4f electrons shield poorly.
bullets: Zr and Hf have almost identical radii.
Basic strength of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La to Lu.
The common oxidation state is +3.

title: Stability patterns in the 3d series
bullets: Mn shows the highest oxidation state, +7.
Cr²⁺ is reducing and Mn³⁺ is oxidising, though both are d⁴.
Cu⁺ disproportionates in water because of the high hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺.
Zn has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation because no d electrons take part in metallic bonding.

title: Werner's theory
bullets: Primary valency is ionisable and matches the oxidation state.
Secondary valency is non-ionisable and equals the coordination number.
Secondary valencies are directional and fix the geometry.

title: Isomerism
bullets: Stereoisomerism: geometrical and optical.
Structural isomerism: linkage, coordination, ionisation and solvate.
cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ is optically active; the trans form is not.

title: Crystal field splitting
content: In an octahedral field, each t₂g electron lowers energy by 0.4Δo and each e_g electron raises it by 0.6Δo. Δt is smaller, so tetrahedral complexes are high spin.

title: Spectrochemical series
content: Ligands arranged in order of increasing field strength, from experimental spectra.
formula: I⁻ < Br⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < S²⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < edta⁴⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO

title: SN1 and SN2
bullets: SN2: one step, back-side attack, inversion of configuration; rate = k[RX][Nu⁻]; reactivity 1° > 2° > 3°.
SN1: two steps through a carbocation, racemisation; rate = k[RX]; reactivity 3° > 2° > 1°.
Leaving group ability: R–I > R–Br > R–Cl > R–F.

title: Halogen exchange
content: NaCl and NaBr are insoluble in dry acetone, which drives the Finkelstein reaction forward.
formula: Finkelstein: R–Cl + NaI → R–I + NaCl (dry acetone) ; Swarts: R–Br + AgF → R–F + AgBr

title: Coupling reactions with sodium
content: All three use sodium in dry ether.
formula: Wurtz: 2RX + 2Na → R–R + 2NaX ; Wurtz–Fittig: ArX + RX + 2Na → Ar–R + 2NaX ; Fittig: 2ArX + 2Na → Ar–Ar + 2NaX

title: Why haloarenes resist nucleophilic substitution
bullets: Resonance gives the C–X bond partial double bond character.
The sp² carbon holds the halogen more tightly.
The phenyl cation is unstable, and the electron-rich ring repels nucleophiles.
–NO₂ groups at ortho and para positions make substitution easier.

title: Dehydration of ethanol
content: Temperature decides the product: lower temperature with excess alcohol gives ether, higher temperature gives alkene.
formula: C₂H₅OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K) ; 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄, 413 K)

title: Williamson synthesis
content: Best with a primary alkyl halide. Tertiary halides give alkenes by elimination.

title: Reactions of phenol
content: The phenoxide ion is highly reactive towards weak electrophiles.
formula: Kolbe: phenol + NaOH, then CO₂ and H⁺ → salicylic acid ; Reimer–Tiemann: phenol + CHCl₃ + aq. NaOH, then H⁺ → salicylaldehyde

title: Acidity of phenols
bullets: Phenol is more acidic than water and alcohols because phenoxide is resonance stabilised.
Electron-withdrawing –NO₂ at ortho or para positions increases acidity.
Electron-releasing –CH₃ decreases acidity.

title: Preparation of aldehydes
content: Palladium on BaSO₄ is partly poisoned, so reduction stops at the aldehyde.
formula: Rosenmund: RCOCl + H₂ → RCHO + HCl (Pd–BaSO₄) ; Stephen: RCN + SnCl₂/HCl, then H₃O⁺ → RCHO

title: Aldol and Cannizzaro reactions
content: Aldol needs an α-hydrogen. Cannizzaro occurs in aldehydes with no α-hydrogen, in concentrated alkali.
formula: 2CH₃CHO → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO → CH₃CH=CHCHO (dil. NaOH, then heat) ; 2HCHO + conc. KOH → CH₃OH + HCOOK

title: Reduction of C=O to CH₂
content: Clemmensen works in acid and Wolff–Kishner in base.
formula: >C=O → >CH₂ (Zn–Hg/conc. HCl) or (NH₂NH₂, then KOH/ethylene glycol, heat)

title: Distinguishing tests
bullets: Tollens' reagent: silver mirror with aldehydes.
Fehling's solution: red-brown Cu₂O with aliphatic aldehydes, not aromatic ones.
Iodoform test: yellow CHI₃ with CH₃CO– compounds.
NaHCO₃: effervescence with carboxylic acids.

title: Acidity of carboxylic acids
content: Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the carboxylate ion and raise acidity.
bullets: FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH > CH₃COOH.
HCOOH is a stronger acid than CH₃COOH.

title: Hofmann bromamide degradation
content: The amine formed has one carbon fewer than the amide.

title: Carbylamine reaction
content: A test for primary amines only. Isocyanides have a foul smell.

title: Diazotisation
content: Arenediazonium salts are made at low temperature and are used at once.

title: Basic strength and Hinsberg's test
bullets: Aqueous order: (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃ and (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃.
Aryl amines are weaker bases than ammonia because the lone pair is delocalised.
Hinsberg: 1° amine product dissolves in alkali, 2° product does not, and 3° amine does not react.

title: Carbohydrates
bullets: Monosaccharides: glucose, fructose.
Disaccharides: sucrose (non-reducing), maltose and lactose (reducing).
Polysaccharides: starch, cellulose, glycogen.

title: Oxidation of glucose
content: Bromine water is a mild oxidant and shows the presence of a –CHO group. Nitric acid also oxidises the terminal –CH₂OH.
formula: Br₂ water: HOCH₂(CHOH)₄CHO → HOCH₂(CHOH)₄COOH (gluconic acid) ; HNO₃: gives HOOC(CHOH)₄COOH (saccharic acid)

title: Structure of proteins
bullets: Primary: sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.
Secondary: α-helix and β-pleated sheet, held by hydrogen bonds.
Tertiary: overall folding; quaternary: arrangement of subunits.
Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structure but leaves the primary structure intact.

title: Nucleic acids
content: A nucleoside is a base plus sugar; a nucleotide also has phosphate. Nucleotides join by 3′–5′ phosphodiester links.
bullets: DNA: 2-deoxyribose with A, G, C, T.
RNA: ribose with A, G, C, U.
Pairing in DNA: A with T, G with C.

title: Vitamins
bullets: Fat soluble: A, D, E, K.
Water soluble: B group and C.
Deficiency: A causes night blindness, C scurvy, D rickets, K increased clotting time.

title: Equivalence relation
content: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on a set A.
bullets: Reflexive: (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A
Symmetric: (a, b) ∈ R ⇒ (b, a) ∈ R
Transitive: (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R

title: One-one and onto functions
bullets: One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂
Onto: every element of the codomain has a preimage
Bijective: one-one and onto together

title: Counting results
content: For finite sets with |A| = m and |B| = n.
formula: Relations A → B: 2^(mn); functions A → B: nᵐ; bijections A → A (|A| = n): n!

title: NCERT: equivalence classes
content: An equivalence relation splits a set into disjoint classes whose union is the whole set. For 'a − b is even' on Z, the classes are the even and the odd integers.

title: Special square matrices
bullets: Symmetric: A′ = A
Skew-symmetric: A′ = −A, so all diagonal entries are 0
Scalar: diagonal with equal diagonal entries; identity I has entries 1

title: Matrix multiplication
content: AB exists when columns of A equal rows of B. Multiplication is not commutative, and AB = O need not mean A = O or B = O.

title: Transpose and inverse laws
content: The order reverses in both cases.

title: Symmetric plus skew-symmetric
content: Every square matrix splits this way, and the split is unique.

title: NCERT: inverse of a matrix
content: A square matrix A is invertible if a matrix B exists with AB = BA = I. If the inverse exists, it is unique.

title: Minors and cofactors
content: The minor Mᵢⱼ is the determinant left after deleting row i and column j.

title: Cofactor and inverse
content: A square matrix is invertible exactly when |A| ≠ 0.

title: Area of a triangle
content: Take the modulus; area is zero when the points are collinear.
formula: Area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|

title: Useful results
content: For a square matrix A of order n.

title: NCERT: solving AX = B
bullets: |A| ≠ 0: unique solution X = A⁻¹B
|A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O: no solution
|A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O: infinitely many or no solutions

title: Continuity at a point
content: f is continuous at x = a when the left limit, the right limit and f(a) all exist and are equal.

title: Continuity versus differentiability
content: Every differentiable function is continuous, but the converse is false: |x| is continuous at 0 yet not differentiable there.

title: Standard derivatives
formula: d/dx(sin⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 − x²); d/dx(tan⁻¹x) = 1/(1 + x²); d/dx(log x) = 1/x; d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ

title: Parametric form
content: For x = f(t), y = g(t) with dx/dt ≠ 0.

title: NCERT: logarithmic differentiation
content: Use it for y = [u(x)]^v(x): take logs, then differentiate implicitly.

title: Coulomb's law
content: Force acts along the line joining two point charges; 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².

title: Electric dipole
content: Field values hold for r ≫ a, with p = q(2a) directed from −q to +q.
formula: E(axial) = 2kp/r³; E(equatorial) = kp/r³; τ = p × E

title: Gauss's law
content: Total flux through a closed surface depends only on the enclosed charge.

title: Gauss's law results
bullets: Infinite line: E = λ/(2πε₀r)
Infinite plane sheet: E = σ/(2ε₀)
Thin shell: E = q/(4πε₀r²) outside, 0 inside

title: NCERT: field line properties
bullets: Start on positive and end on negative charges
Two lines never cross
Electrostatic field lines do not form closed loops

title: Potential of a point charge
content: Potential is a scalar, so add values with their signs.

title: Equipotential surfaces
content: No work is done moving a charge along an equipotential surface, and the field is perpendicular to it at every point.

title: Capacitors
content: K is the dielectric constant of the material filling the gap.
formula: C = Kε₀A/d; series 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂; parallel C = C₁ + C₂

title: NCERT: inserting a dielectric
bullets: Battery removed: Q fixed, V → V/K, U → U/K
Battery connected: V fixed, Q → KQ, U → KU
C → KC in both cases

title: Drift and current
content: n is the free electron density, τ the relaxation time and μ the mobility.
formula: I = neAv_d; v_d = eEτ/m; μ = v_d/E = eτ/m

title: Resistance and resistivity
formula: R = ρl/A; ρ = m/(ne²τ); ρ_T = ρ₀[1 + α(T − T₀)]

title: Cell and power
content: r is the internal resistance; V is the terminal voltage on discharge.
formula: V = ε − Ir; P = VI = I²R = V²/R

title: Kirchhoff's rules and bridge
bullets: Junction rule: sum of currents in = sum out (charge conservation)
Loop rule: algebraic sum of potential changes is zero (energy conservation)
Wheatstone bridge balance: P/Q = R/S

title: NCERT: combination of cells
bullets: Series: ε(eq) = ε₁ + ε₂, r(eq) = r₁ + r₂
Parallel: ε(eq)/r(eq) = ε₁/r₁ + ε₂/r₂
Parallel: 1/r(eq) = 1/r₁ + 1/r₂

title: Spherical mirrors
content: Use the Cartesian sign convention, measuring from the pole.

title: Total internal reflection
content: It occurs when light goes from denser to rarer medium with i greater than the critical angle, where sin i_c = 1/n. Optical fibres work on this principle.

title: Prism
content: D_m is the angle of minimum deviation and A is the prism angle.

title: NCERT: magnifying power
bullets: Compound microscope: m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e)
Telescope, normal adjustment: m = f_o/f_e
Telescope tube length: f_o + f_e

title: Microsporangium wall
content: Four wall layers surround the sporogenous tissue.
bullets: Epidermis, endothecium and middle layers: protection and dehiscence
Tapetum: innermost layer that nourishes developing pollen

title: Mature embryo sac
content: The Polygonum type is 7-celled and 8-nucleate, formed from one functional megaspore.
bullets: Egg apparatus: egg and 2 synergids
3 antipodals at the chalazal end
Central cell with 2 polar nuclei

title: Types of pollination
bullets: Autogamy: within the same flower
Geitonogamy: another flower of the same plant
Xenogamy: flower of a different plant

title: Double fertilisation
content: Syngamy and triple fusion occur in the same embryo sac.
formula: Male gamete + egg → zygote (2n); male gamete + 2 polar nuclei → PEN (3n)

title: NCERT: apomixis and polyembryony
content: Apomixis produces seeds without fertilisation. In Citrus and mango, some nucellar cells protrude into the embryo sac and form extra embryos.

title: Cells of the testis
bullets: Spermatogonia: divide to form sperm
Sertoli cells: nourish germ cells
Leydig cells: interstitial, secrete androgens

title: Spermatogenesis
content: Spermiogenesis converts spermatids into spermatozoa.
formula: Spermatogonium (2n) → primary spermatocyte (2n) → secondary spermatocytes (n) → spermatids (n) → spermatozoa (n)

title: Menstrual cycle
bullets: Menstrual phase: endometrium breaks down
Follicular phase: FSH and oestrogen, endometrium regenerates
Ovulation: LH surge near day 14
Luteal phase: corpus luteum secretes progesterone

title: Implantation
content: Attachment of the blastocyst to the endometrium through the trophoblast, which leads to pregnancy.

title: NCERT: hormones of pregnancy
content: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces hCG, hPL, oestrogens and progestogens. Relaxin is produced by the ovary in the later phase of pregnancy.

title: Mendel's laws
bullets: Dominance: one factor expresses over the other
Segregation: alleles separate during gamete formation
Independent assortment: gene pairs segregate independently

title: Key ratios
formula: Monohybrid F₂ 3:1 (genotypic 1:2:1); dihybrid F₂ 9:3:3:1; monohybrid test cross 1:1

title: Beyond simple dominance
bullets: Incomplete dominance: F₂ snapdragon ratio 1:2:1
Codominance: IᴬIᴮ gives blood group AB
Linkage: genes on one chromosome tend to stay together

title: Sex determination
bullets: Grasshopper: XX female, XO male
Humans and Drosophila: XX female, XY male
Birds: ZW female, ZZ male

title: NCERT: genetic disorders
bullets: X-linked recessive: haemophilia, colour blindness
Sickle cell anaemia: autosomal recessive
Down's syndrome: trisomy 21
Klinefelter's: 47, XXY; Turner's: 45, X0

title: DNA double helix
bullets: Two antiparallel polynucleotide chains
A pairs with T by 2 H-bonds; G with C by 3
Pitch 3.4 nm, about 10 bp per turn, rise 0.34 nm per bp

title: Central dogma
content: Information generally flows from DNA to RNA to protein.

title: DNA replication
bullets: Semiconservative, shown by Meselson and Stahl using ¹⁵N
Leading strand is continuous; lagging strand forms Okazaki fragments
DNA ligase joins the fragments

title: Lac operon
bullets: i gene makes the repressor
z, y, a make β-galactosidase, permease, transacetylase
Lactose acts as inducer by inactivating the repressor

title: NCERT: genetic code
bullets: Triplet code with 64 codons; 61 code for amino acids
AUG is the start codon and codes for methionine
UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons
Degenerate, unambiguous and nearly universal

title: Polynomial and degree
content: A polynomial in one variable has terms of the form axⁿ, where n is a whole number. The degree is the highest power of the variable.
bullets: Degree 1: linear
Degree 2: quadratic
Degree 3: cubic

title: Zero of a polynomial
content: A real number a is a zero of p(x) if p(a) = 0.
bullets: A linear polynomial has exactly one zero
A non-zero constant polynomial has no zero
Every real number is a zero of the zero polynomial

title: Factor Theorem
content: Use it to test a possible factor by substitution.
formula: x − a is a factor of p(x) ⇔ p(a) = 0

title: Key identities
content: These give quick expansions and factorisations.
formula: (x + y + z)² = x² + y² + z² + 2xy + 2yz + 2zx; x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx)

title: Splitting the middle term
content: To factorise ax² + bx + c, find p and q with p + q = b and pq = ac.

title: Right circular cone: surface
content: Slant height links the radius and the height by Pythagoras.
formula: l = √(r² + h²); CSA = πrl; TSA = πr(l + r)

title: Sphere and hemisphere: surface
content: A solid hemisphere's total surface includes its flat circular base.
formula: Sphere S = 4πr²; Hemisphere CSA = 2πr²; Hemisphere TSA = 3πr²

title: Volumes
content: All volumes are in cubic units.
formula: Cone V = ⅓πr²h; Sphere V = (4/3)πr³; Hemisphere V = (2/3)πr³

title: Cone and cylinder
content: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height.
bullets: Take π = 22/7 unless told otherwise
Melting and recasting keeps the volume unchanged

title: Sub-atomic particles
bullets: Electron: charge −1, discovered by J.J. Thomson
Proton: charge +1, canal rays observed by E. Goldstein
Neutron: no charge, discovered by J. Chadwick

title: Rutherford's alpha-scattering results
content: Most alpha particles passed straight through gold foil, some deflected, and about 1 in 12000 rebounded.
bullets: Most of the atom is empty space
A small, dense, positive nucleus holds nearly all the mass

title: Bohr-Bury shell rule
content: Shells fill stepwise, and the outermost shell holds at most 8 electrons.
formula: Maximum electrons in shell n = 2n² (K = 2, L = 8, M = 18, N = 32)

title: Atomic and mass number
content: Atomic number Z is the number of protons. Mass number A is protons plus neutrons.
bullets: Isotopes: same Z, different A
Isobars: same A, different Z

title: Valency
content: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom, from the electrons lost, gained or shared to complete the octet.
bullets: Na: 1
Mg: 2
Cl: 1

title: Distance and displacement
content: Distance is the actual path length. Displacement is the shortest distance from start to end, with direction.

title: Speed, velocity, acceleration
bullets: Speed = distance / time
Velocity = displacement / time
Acceleration = change in velocity / time

title: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion
content: Here u is initial velocity, v final velocity, a acceleration, s displacement and t time.
formula: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; 2as = v² − u²

title: Reading graphs
bullets: Slope of a distance-time graph gives speed
Slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration
Area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement

title: Standard form
content: A quadratic equation is ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. A root is a value of x that satisfies it.

title: Quadratic formula
content: It gives the roots whenever b² − 4ac ≥ 0.

title: Discriminant and nature of roots
bullets: D > 0: two distinct real roots
D = 0: two equal real roots
D < 0: no real roots

title: Factorisation method
content: Split the middle term so the two parts multiply to ac and add to b, then set each factor to zero.

title: Trigonometric ratios
content: In a right triangle, ratios are defined for an acute angle A from its sides.
bullets: sin A = opposite / hypotenuse
cos A = adjacent / hypotenuse
tan A = opposite / adjacent

title: Standard values
content: Recall these for 30°, 45° and 60°.

title: Identities
content: These hold for every acute angle A where the terms are defined.
formula: sin²A + cos²A = 1; 1 + tan²A = sec²A; 1 + cot²A = cosec²A

title: Reciprocal and quotient relations
bullets: cosec A = 1/sin A
sec A = 1/cos A
cot A = 1/tan A
tan A = sin A / cos A

title: Balancing equations
content: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed, so each element must have equal atoms on both sides. This follows the law of conservation of mass.

title: Combination (exothermic)
content: Quicklime reacts vigorously with water to give slaked lime.

title: Thermal decomposition
content: Heating green ferrous sulphate leaves a brown solid and gives a smell of burning sulphur.

title: Displacement and double displacement
content: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one; in double displacement, ions are exchanged.
formula: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu; Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl

title: Oxidation and reduction
content: Oxidation is gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen; reduction is the reverse.
bullets: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, copper oxide is reduced
Hydrogen is oxidised to water

title: Ohm's law and resistance
content: At constant temperature, current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference. Resistivity ρ depends on the material.

title: Combinations of resistors
content: Series adds resistance; parallel lowers the total below the smallest resistor.

title: Heating and power
content: Joule's law gives the heat produced in a resistor.
formula: H = I²Rt; P = VI = I²R = V²/R

title: Charge and potential difference
content: Current is the charge flowing per unit time, Q = It. Potential difference is the work done per unit charge, V = W/Q.

title: Practical points
bullets: Connect an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel
1 kWh = 1 unit = 3.6 × 10⁶ J
Household appliances are wired in parallel

title: Representing sets
content: Roster form lists the elements. Set-builder form states a common property.
bullets: Roster: {1, 2, 3}
Set-builder: {x : x ∈ N, x < 4}

title: Subsets and the universal set
content: A ⊂ B if every element of A is in B. The empty set is a subset of every set.

title: Intervals
content: Round brackets exclude an endpoint; square brackets include it.

title: De Morgan's laws
content: Complement swaps union and intersection.

title: Difference and complement
bullets: A − B = {x : x ∈ A and x ∉ B}
A′ = U − A

title: Limit of a function
content: lim(x→a) f(x) = L exists when the left-hand and right-hand limits both equal L.

title: Standard limits
content: Angles are in radians.
formula: lim(x→a) (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = naⁿ⁻¹; lim(x→0) sin x/x = 1; lim(x→0) (1 − cos x)/x = 0

title: Derivative from first principles
content: The derivative is the limit of the difference quotient.

title: Rules of differentiation
bullets: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹
d/dx(sin x) = cos x
d/dx(cos x) = −sin x

title: Algebra of limits
content: Limits of a sum, difference, product and quotient equal the same operation on the limits, when the denominator's limit is non-zero.

title: Newton's laws
bullets: First: a body keeps its state of rest or uniform motion unless a net external force acts
Second: force equals rate of change of momentum
Third: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction

title: Force and impulse
content: Impulse is the product of force and time, and it equals the change in momentum.
formula: F = dp/dt = ma; Impulse = FΔt = Δp

title: Friction and level circular road
content: Static friction adjusts up to a limit; on a level curve it supplies the centripetal force.

title: Action-reaction and momentum
content: Action and reaction act on different bodies, so they never cancel each other.
bullets: Total momentum of an isolated system stays constant

title: Work by a constant force
content: Work is the scalar product of force and displacement.
formula: W = F · d = Fd cos θ

title: Work-energy theorem
content: Net work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.

title: Potential energy and power
content: Gravitational and spring forces are conservative.
formula: V = mgh; V_spring = ½kx²; P = W/t = F · v

title: Collisions
content: Linear momentum is conserved in all collisions.
bullets: Elastic: kinetic energy is also conserved
Inelastic: some kinetic energy is lost
Completely inelastic: the bodies stick together

title: The mole
content: One mole contains exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities, the Avogadro constant.

title: Mole relations
content: Here m is mass, M molar mass, N number of particles and Nₐ the Avogadro constant.
bullets: Molecular formula = empirical formula × (molar mass / empirical formula mass)

title: Concentration terms
content: Molarity uses litres of solution; molality uses kilograms of solvent.
formula: M = moles of solute / L of solution; m = moles of solute / kg of solvent; mass % = (mass of solute / mass of solution) × 100

title: Laws of chemical combination
bullets: Conservation of mass
Definite proportions
Multiple proportions
Gay Lussac's law of gaseous volumes
Avogadro's law

title: Limiting reagent
content: The reactant used up first limits the amount of product formed.

title: Formal charge and dipole moment
content: V is valence electrons, L is lone-pair electrons and S is shared electrons on the atom.
formula: Formal charge = V − L − ½S; μ = Q × r

title: VSEPR repulsion order
content: Lone pairs repel more strongly than bond pairs and shrink bond angles.
bullets: lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp
NH₃ 107°

title: Hybridisation and shape
bullets: sp: linear, 180°
sp²: trigonal planar, 120°
sp³: tetrahedral, 109.5°
sp³d: trigonal bipyramidal
sp³d²: octahedral

title: Bond order
content: Nb and Na are electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals. Higher bond order means a shorter, stronger bond.

title: Molecular orbital results
bullets: N₂ has bond order 3 and is diamagnetic
O₂ has bond order 2 and is paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons
A positive bond order (Nb > Na) indicates a stable molecule

title: Cell theory
content: Schleiden and Schwann proposed that all living organisms are made of cells. Virchow added that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
bullets: Omnis cellula-e cellula

title: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
content: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles. Eukaryotes have both.
bullets: Prokaryotes: bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma
Eukaryotes: protists, fungi, plants, animals

title: Ribosome types
content: S stands for the Svedberg unit, a measure of sedimentation.

title: Fluid mosaic model
content: Singer and Nicolson (1972) described the membrane as a quasi-fluid lipid bilayer with proteins.
bullets: Proteins are integral or peripheral
Fluidity aids growth, secretion and division

title: Organelle roles
bullets: Golgi: packaging, glycoproteins and glycolipids
Lysosome: hydrolytic digestion
Mitochondrion: aerobic respiration, ATP
Chloroplast: photosynthesis

title: Composition of blood
content: Plasma forms about 55% of blood and formed elements about 45%.
bullets: RBCs live about 120 days
Normal haemoglobin is 12–16 g per 100 mL
Blood groups: A, B, AB, O

title: Cardiac output
content: It is the blood pumped by each ventricle per minute, about 5 L in a healthy adult.
formula: Cardiac output = Stroke volume × Heart rate ≈ 70 mL × 72 per min ≈ 5 L/min

title: Cardiac cycle
content: One cycle of systole and diastole of the atria and ventricles lasts 0.8 s at 75 beats per minute.
bullets: Lub: closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves
Dub: closure of the semilunar valves

title: Conducting system and ECG
content: The SA node is the pacemaker, generating 70–75 action potentials per minute.
bullets: P wave: atrial depolarisation
QRS complex: ventricular depolarisation
T wave: ventricular repolarisation
